subject: SOC 2 renewal — staging plan, archival access window, and burst capacity request
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@grayboxaudit.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 renewal — staging plan, archival access window, and burst capacity request

Hi Liam,

Per Acme Payments' renewal schedule, we expect the formal SOC 2 re-attestation to kick off in early September. To make the evidence handoff predictable for your team (and to avoid last-minute scaling tickets), I put together a proposed staging plan and a short ask for a temporary burst capacity window on our side. Attached: evidence_index_2026-08-10.csv and staging_timeline_v2.xlsx.

Key asks from our side:
- A 72-hour archival access window (read-only) for your engineers to pull raw logs from the retention archive (anticipated dates: Sep 6–8).
- A short-term burst allocation: +30% token throughput for the week of Sep 6 to handle exported log processing.
- Confirmation of the evidence extraction format you prefer (CSV vs NDJSON) and any file size limits.

High-level timeline:
- Aug 10–20: Evidence curation and tagging (we'll upload to shared Drive).
- Aug 23–Sep 1: Staging handoff and dry-run.
- Sep 6–8: Audit access window + extraction.

Can you confirm whether the 72-hour window and the temporary burst are acceptable? If you prefer, we can stage a one-hour dry-run earlier (Aug 27) to validate access and formats.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Customer Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
[attachment: evidence_index_2026-08-10.csv (csv)]

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@grayboxaudit.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: audit-team@grayboxaudit.com, security@acmepayments.com (Laura Chen)
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SOC 2 renewal — staging plan, archival access window, and burst capacity request

Mina,

Thanks for the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side before I confirm the access window:
1) File format: NDJSON is preferred for event logs (one JSON obj per line). Small supporting artifacts (config exports, manifests) can be CSV.
2) We will accept the 72-hour read-only window. For the burst allocation, we need an estimate of expected peak export I/O and total bytes to be pulled so we can size our parallel workers.
3) For the dry-run on Aug 27 — that's helpful. Please include an authentication test token and a sample NDJSON file in the Drive link beforehand so we can validate ingestion.

Can you send the expected export size and a short summary of how the archived logs are partitioned (by tenant / region / day)? Also, please add Connor from your infra team to the thread so we can coordinate bandwidth throttles.

Best,
Liam O'Neill
Senior Auditor, GrayBox Audit
[signature: Liam O'Neill | liam.oneill@grayboxaudit.com]
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@grayboxaudit.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 renewal — staging plan, archival access window, and burst capacity request

Thanks, Liam — appreciate the quick review. Details below:

Export format and partitioning
- Primary logs: NDJSON, partitioned by date (YYYY-MM-DD) and region (us/eu). Each file is ~150–350 MB compressed; daily volume for Acme Payments is ~45 GB (compressed).
- Supporting artifacts (manifests, config snapshots): CSV/TSV, typical size <5 MB each.

Burst capacity ask (our internal numbers)
- Expected peak export I/O to support GrayBox parallel workers: ~550 MB/s sustained over 6 hours for bulk pulls.
- Total bytes for the planned 72-hour window (estimated): 320 GB compressed (tenant: acme-prod).

Dry-run actions (proposed Aug 27, 09:00–10:00 PDT)
- Deliverables: sample NDJSON (1 day), an auth test token valid for 2 hours, and the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cEvidenceMap
- Success criteria: GrayBox can ingest sample NDJSON within 20 minutes and validate manifest checksums.

Attachments: burst_capacity_model.pdf (breakdown of the throughput assumptions and how we can throttle).

If this looks good, can you confirm the number of parallel workers you'll employ so we can finalize the I/O reservation?

Mina
[attachment: burst_capacity_model.pdf (pdf)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@grayboxaudit.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 renewal — staging plan, archival access window, and burst capacity request

Looping in a quick cost/commit note — Mina, Connor: the +30% token throughput and a 6-hour 550 MB/s sustained window maps to approximately a one-week incremental commit on our Dedicated capacity plan given current utilization.

Questions for sizing the commercial ask:
- Is it possible to run the bulk pulls in a narrower window (e.g., 4 hours) if GrayBox can add more parallel workers? That would reduce the length of the burst.
- If we need to extend beyond the 72-hr access (for re-runs), will Acme accept a staged billing amendment or should we bake this into the renewal amendment now?

Kim — can you confirm we have pricing flexibility for a short-term burst add-on versus rolling it into the annual term amendment?

—Ben
Head of Customer Reliability Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@grayboxaudit.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 renewal — staging plan, archival access window, and burst capacity request

Liam / Acme Security team — thank you for the prompt coordination.

We can commit to the Aug 27 dry-run and the Sep 6–8 72-hour read-only window. Regarding burst capacity: we will provision a targeted +30% token throughput reservation for Sep 6–8. If GrayBox increases parallelism and completes ingestion in a 4-hour window, we will pro-rate the burst cost to Acme for the shorter reservation (Ben, finance will invoice a usage-based addendum).

Next steps (action owners):
- Mina: finalize Drive uploads and drop sample NDJSON + test token by Aug 24.
- Connor: schedule the infra reservation and confirm throttles; provide exact I/O limits by Aug 18.
- Liam: let us know planned number of parallel workers and preferred manifest checksum algorithm (md5 / sha256).
- Ben: draft short-term addendum language for burst billing and share for approval by Aug 20.

I'll also start a DocuSign envelope for the small amendment (link below) to capture the surge addendum and the archival access clause so we don't lose timeline.

DocuSign: https://app.redwood.com/contracts/ACME-2026-RENEW/docuSign

Thanks all — Kim
VP, Customer Success & Renewals
Redwood Inference
